literal: In the tenth month of winter, on day wuyin, Cige captured Pingzhou; on returning, he again rebelled with Dieci, Yindishi, Anduan, and others.
idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, on wuyin day, Cige took Pingzhou; coming back, he rose again with Dieci, Yindishi, Anduan, and the rest.

literal: On day jiashen, envoys were dispatched to Liang to present sacrificial offerings.
idiomatic: On jiashen day he sent envoys to Liang with offerings for the rites.

literal: On day renchen, returning he halted at North Aru Mountain; hearing his younger brothers had blocked the road with troops, he led the army south toward the Seventeen Marshes.
idiomatic: On renchen day, marching back, he encamped at North Aru Mountain. Learning that his brothers had barred the route with soldiers, he turned the army south toward the Seventeen Marshes.

literal: That day he burned sacrificial wood.
idiomatic: That day he performed the burnt-offering rite.

literal: The next day, he halted at the Seven Crossings River; each of his younger brothers sent someone to apologize.
idiomatic: The following day he stopped at the Seven Crossings River, and each brother dispatched a messenger to beg forgiveness.

literal: The Emperor still showed compassion and granted them permission to reform themselves.
idiomatic: The Emperor still looked on them with pity and allowed them to start anew.

literal: That year, with troops he campaigned against Liangye; bringing back the fifty captives including the monk Chongwen to Xilou, he built Tianxiong Temple to house them, as a sign that Heaven aided martial prowess.
idiomatic: That year he took the field against Liangye. The fifty prisoners he won, among them the monk Chongwen, he brought back to Xilou and settled in a new Tianxiong Temple, proclaiming Heaven's blessing on his arms.

literal: In the seventh year, on the jiachen new moon of the first spring month, court audience was dispensed with because of military operations.
idiomatic: In the seventh year, on the jiachen new moon of the first spring month, the regular levee was canceled for war.

literal: Prince of Jin Li Cunxu besieged Youzhou and captured Liu Shouguang.
idiomatic: Li Cunxu, Prince of Jin, invested Youzhou and took Liu Shouguang prisoner.

literal: On day jiayin, the imperial army halted at Chishui City; his younger brother Cige and others begged to surrender.
idiomatic: On jiayin day the royal host encamped at Chishui City, and Cige and his brothers sued for surrender.

literal: The Emperor wore plain white dress, mounted a reddish-white horse, and with Generals Yelü Legu and Xiala Jinebo as escorts, laid aside weapons and cleared his guard to receive them, then offered words of comfort and instruction.
idiomatic: The Emperor put on undyed robes, rode a sorrel-white horse, and with Generals Yelü Legu and Xiala Jinebo at his side laid down arms and thinned his guard to receive them, then spoke to them in reassurance.

literal: Cige and the others withdrew; the Emperor again repeatedly sent envoys to console them.
idiomatic: Cige and the rest withdrew, and the Emperor sent envoy after envoy to soothe them.

literal: On the jiaxu new moon of the second month, Liang's Prince of Jun Zhu Youzhen overthrew and killed his elder brother Zhu Yougui and succeeded to the throne.
idiomatic: On the jiaxu new moon of the second month, Zhu Youzhen, Liang's Prince of Jun, struck down his elder brother Zhu Yougui and seized the throne.

literal: In the third month, on day guichou, he halted at Lu River; his younger brother Dieci Getu, installed as King of Xi, arrived with Anduan leading more than a thousand horsemen, falsely claiming to come for an audience.
idiomatic: In the third month, on guichou day, he stopped at Lu River. His brother Dieci Getu, now styled King of Xi, came up with Anduan at the head of more than a thousand riders, pretending he meant to attend court.

literal: The Emperor angrily said: "You at first plotted rebellion and disorder; I especially forgave you, that you might amend your faults and renew yourselves—yet you still waver and turn back; you mean harm to me!
idiomatic: The Emperor flared in anger: "You first conspired in treason; I alone spared you so you might repent and reform—and still you turn and turn again, plotting against my person!

literal: " He thereupon had them seized.
idiomatic: " At once he had them seized.

literal: Their followers were assigned to the various armies.
idiomatic: Their men were distributed among the regiments.

literal: Meanwhile Cige led his followers to Yisijin Marsh, displayed the imperial banners and drums, and was about to declare himself emperor; the Empress Dowager secretly sent someone instructing them to withdraw.
idiomatic: Meanwhile Cige marched his force to Yisijin Marsh, raised the imperial banners and drums, and prepared to proclaim himself ruler; the Empress Dowager secretly sent word telling them to fall back.

literal: When Migunai and Huailiyang reported that the imperial carriage was about to arrive, his force panicked and scattered, plundered the populace and fled north; the Emperor pursued with troops.
idiomatic: Migunai and Huailiyang cried that the imperial train was near; the rebels broke in panic, looted the people, and fled north, and the Emperor gave chase with his army.

literal: Cige sent his partisan Yindishi to lead troops straight to the traveling palace, burned its baggage and tents, and let his soldiers slaughter freely.
idiomatic: Cige sent his follower Yindishi straight at the traveling palace with troops, burned wagons and tents, and turned his men loose to kill at will.

literal: The empress urgently dispatched Shugulu to rescue it; <6> they recovered only the imperial banners and drums.
idiomatic: The Empress hurried Shugulu to the rescue; <6> he salvaged nothing but the imperial banners and drums.

literal: His partisan Senshengu again raided Xilou and burned the Bright King Tower.
idiomatic: Another rebel, Senshengu, struck Xilou again and put the Bright King Tower to the torch.

literal: The Emperor reached Tu River, fed the horses and rested the troops, as though unconcerned.
idiomatic: The Emperor came to Tu River, watered the horses and rested the men, showing no sign of alarm.

literal: The generals urged immediate pursuit; the Emperor said: "Wait until they have fled far away; each man will yearn for home.
idiomatic: His generals pressed for a hot pursuit, but the Emperor said: "Let them run far first; every man will begin to long for home.

literal: When homesickness grows acute, their hearts will surely split apart; our army will seize the moment—defeat is certain!
idiomatic: When that longing bites deep, their hearts will break apart; then our troops will strike, and victory is assured!

literal: " He distributed all the livestock and goods taken earlier among officers and soldiers, and left Yilie Bilizhili in charge of government affairs.
idiomatic: " He gave out all the herds and goods seized earlier to officers and rank and file alike, and left Yilie Bilizhili to govern affairs.

literal: In the fourth month of summer, on day wuyin, he pursued Cige northward.
idiomatic: In the fourth summer month, on wuyin day, he pressed north after Cige.

literal: On day jimao, he halted at Mili; inquiring about how his younger brothers, facing Mount Muye, shot ghost-arrows for exorcism, <7> he then seized the rebel Jieli and directed him there, likewise using that method to curse him.
idiomatic: On jimao day he encamped at Mili. Learning how his brothers had faced Mount Muye and shot ghost-arrows to ward off evil, <7> he seized the rebel Jieli and sent him thither, treating him to the same rite of curse.

literal: Reaching Dali Marsh, he chose light cavalry and pursued to Peizhi River, capturing all their party's baggage and captives.
idiomatic: At Dali Marsh he picked out light horsemen and ran the fugitives down to Peizhi River, taking all their baggage and prisoners.

literal: He first sent five chiefs including the Shiwei and Tuguhun leaders Bola and Diligu to divide forces and ambush their forward route, ordering the Northern Chancellor Diligu as vanguard to advance and attack.
idiomatic: First he posted five chieftains, among them the Shiwei and Tuguhun leaders Bola and Diligu, to split their men and lie in wait along the road ahead, while Northern Chancellor Diligu led the van in attack.

literal: Cige led troops to meet in battle; Diligu closed with light forces.
idiomatic: Cige turned to fight; Diligu pressed him with a light detachment.

literal: His younger brother Eguzhi on the battle line shot down dozens of men; none dared advance.
idiomatic: His brother Eguzhi stood in the front rank and dropped dozens of men; no one dared press forward.

literal: They contested until late afternoon, then his force collapsed.
idiomatic: The standoff lasted until dusk, then the rebel line gave way.

literal: Pursuit reached Chai River; they then burned their own carts, tents, and departed.
idiomatic: The chase carried to Chai River; there the rebels burned their own wagons and tents and fled on.

literal: Ahead they met Bola, Diligu, and the other ambush as it sprang; combined attack then routed them utterly.
idiomatic: Farther on they ran into Bola, Diligu, and the rest as the ambush closed; the converging blow shattered them completely.

literal: Cige fled in rout and abandoned on the road the divine tent he had seized; the Emperor saw it and bowed in offering.
idiomatic: Cige broke and ran, leaving on the road the sacred tent he had stolen; the Emperor came upon it and bowed in reverent offering.

literal: All captives taken were released to return to their homelands.
idiomatic: Every prisoner taken was freed to go home.

literal: His partisans Kuguzhi and Moduo were all bound facing forward and begged for pardon.
idiomatic: His followers Kuguzhi and Moduo came forward with hands bound and pleaded for mercy.

literal: The army halted at Zhadu River; great rain swelled the waters suddenly.
idiomatic: The host stopped at Zhadu River as a cloudburst sent the stream raging.

literal: In the fifth month, on day guichou, he sent the Northern Chancellor Dilian leading crack horsemen to cross first.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guichou day, he sent Northern Chancellor Dilian with elite cavalry to ford ahead.

literal: On day jiayin, it was reported that Cige and Nielihun A'bo were captured at Yu River; the former Northern Chancellor Xiao Shilu and Yindishi cut their own throats but did not die.
idiomatic: On jiayin day came word that Cige and Nielihun A'bo had been taken at Yu River; the former Northern Chancellor Xiao Shilu and Yindishi had slashed their own throats but survived.

literal: Thereupon black and white sheep were used to sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.
idiomatic: Black and white sheep were then offered to Heaven and Earth.

literal: On day renxu, Cige and Nielihun A'bo came to the traveling court, bound themselves with straw ropes, led sheep and bowed from afar.
idiomatic: On renxu day Cige and Nielihun A'bo appeared at the traveling court with straw cords about them, sheep in hand, bowing from a distance.

literal: The Emperor returned to Dal Ling.
idiomatic: The Emperor came back to Dal Ling.

literal: At that time the great army had been long abroad; baggage trains were not linked; soldiers boiled foals and gathered wild vegetables for food; livestock dying on the road were seven or eight in ten; prices rose tenfold; weapons, garments, goods and wealth were abandoned at Chuli River, scattered for hundreds of li; therefore Cige's name was changed to Baoli.
idiomatic: The main army had been away too long; supply trains had fallen apart; men boiled colts and foraged wild greens to eat; seven or eight of every ten beasts died on the march; prices soared tenfold; arms, dress, goods, and treasure lay abandoned along Chuli River for hundreds of li in wreckage—and so Cige was renamed Baoli.

literal: On day bingyin, reaching Kuli, he sacrificed with a blue ox and white horse to Heaven and Earth.
idiomatic: On bingyin day, arriving at Kuli, he offered a blue ox and a white horse to Heaven and Earth.

literal: Six hundred captives and two thousand three hundred horses were distributed as rewards to the Greater and Lesser Hawk Armies.
idiomatic: Six hundred prisoners and twenty-three hundred horses were divided as booty between the Greater and Lesser Hawk Armies.

literal: In the sixth month, on day xinsi, reaching Yu Ling, because Saogu of Xialai County illegally tyrannized the people, he was dismembered.
idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinsi day, at Yu Ling, Saogu of Xialai County was torn apart for oppressing the people by unlawful means.

literal: On day jiashen, the Emperor ascended Du'an Mountain, touched the traces left by the former Qishi Khan, and wandered looking back, sighing with emotion.
idiomatic: On jiashen day the Emperor climbed Du'an Mountain, lingered over the relics of the first Qishi Khan, and paced there looking back, moved to deep sighs.

literal: Hearing the prison officer Nieli had arbitrarily devised a great cangue, people could not bear the suffering and some died from it; he ordered him executed.
idiomatic: Learning that the jailer Nieli had on his own authority fashioned a massive cangue, torment so fierce that men died under it, he ordered Nieli put to death.

literal: On day renchen, he halted at Lang River; captured rebels Yali and Mili were buried alive beneath the rails south of the Tong River.
idiomatic: On renchen day he encamped at Lang River; the captured rebels Yali and Mili were buried alive under the track south of the Tong River.

literal: Released captives were sent back; many were seized by the Yuguri.
idiomatic: Freed prisoners were sent on their way, but many were snatched up again by the Yuguri.

literal: The Emperor in anger led light cavalry in swift attack.
idiomatic: Enraged, the Emperor himself galloped out with light horse to strike them.

literal: He again sent crack generals on separate routes to pursue and raid, capturing all their force together with the plunderers.
idiomatic: He then sent fierce commanders by separate paths to hunt them down, taking every man of theirs along with the looters.

literal: On day gengzi, he halted at Adun Marsh; because his adopted son Nielisi had joined the younger brothers in rebellion, he was shot to death with ghost-arrows.
idiomatic: On gengzi day he stopped at Adun Marsh; his adopted son Nielisi, who had sided with the rebel brothers, was executed by ghost-arrow.

literal: The remaining six thousand partisans were each sentenced according to the severity of their crimes.
idiomatic: Six thousand remaining accomplices were punished each according to the weight of his offense.

literal: More than thirty of the Yuqi who had seized captives were also allowed to ransom their guilt and were released to their districts.
idiomatic: Thirty-odd Yuqi who had carried off prisoners were likewise permitted to buy back their guilt and return to their tribes.

literal: Reaching west of Shiling, he ordered recovered the weapons abandoned when the returning army lacked food, summoned Northern Prefecture soldiers to verify and return them.
idiomatic: West of Shiling he commanded that arms cast aside for want of food on the march home be gathered in; Northern Prefecture troops were called to identify and reclaim them.

literal: Because Yilie Nielihun had joined the younger brothers in rebellion, unable to bear public execution, he was ordered to throw himself from a cliff and die.
idiomatic: Yilie Nielihun, who had followed the brothers into revolt, the Emperor could not bear to kill before the court; he was commanded to cast himself from a cliff.

literal: In the eighth month of autumn, on day jimao, he visited Longmei Palace; twenty-nine rebels—their wives and daughters were bestowed on meritorious officers and commanders; stolen treasures and livestock were returned to owners;
idiomatic: In the eighth autumn month, on jimao day, he went to Longmei Palace. Twenty-nine rebels' wives and daughters were given to deserving officers; plundered gems and herds were restored to their owners;

literal: those who had lost their original goods were ordered to make restitution to their households;
idiomatic: where the original property was gone, the culprits were ordered to compensate the households;

literal: those who could not pay were granted the rebel's followers in compensation.
idiomatic: those who could not pay were awarded the rebels' retainers in lieu.

literal: In the ninth month, on day renxu, the Emperor departed from Xilou.
idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renxu day, the Emperor set out from Xilou.

literal: In the tenth month of winter, on day gengwu.
idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, on gengwu day.

literal: He encamped at Chiya.
idiomatic: He made camp at Chiya.

literal: On day wuyin, the Huihu of Hezhou came to pay tribute.
idiomatic: On wuyin day the Uighurs of Hezhou arrived with tribute.

literal: On day guimwei, Diligu of Yishi Prefecture and Teli of the Migulii tribe were executed for joining the rebellion.
idiomatic: On guimwei day Diligu of Yishi Prefecture and Teli of the Migulii tribe were put to death for following the revolt.

literal: He decreed that ministers divide and decide backlogged lawsuits; Han Zhigu was to record the proceedings; Zhiliggu was to manage the pursuit of fugitives.
idiomatic: He ordered the ministers to divide and clear stalled cases; Han Zhigu was to keep the record, and Zhiliggu to hunt down fugitives.

literal: In the eleventh month, he sacrificed at Mount Muye.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month he offered sacrifice at Mount Muye.

literal: Returning he halted at Zhaowu Mountain, inspected local customs, received the aged, discussed court policy, and fixed auspicious and inauspicious rites.
idiomatic: On the return he stopped at Zhaowu Mountain, reviewed local ways, received the elderly, debated state affairs, and settled the rites of fortune and misfortune.

literal: In the twelfth month, on day wuzi, he burned sacrificial wood at Lotus Marsh.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuzi day, he burned sacrificial wood at Lotus Marsh.

literal: In the eighth year, on day jiachen in the first month of spring, Helu was made Yilie of the Yelie Tribe, and Hulie was made Tiyin.
idiomatic: In the eighth year, on jiachen day of the first spring month, Helu was appointed yilie of the Yelie tribe and Hulie was made tiyin.

literal: Telimin of the Yuguri tribe seized rebel partisans Buhu, Yalizhi, and seventeen others and presented them; the Emperor personally interrogated them.
idiomatic: Telimin of the Yuguri tribe captured seventeen rebels including Buhu and Yalizhi and brought them in; the Emperor examined them himself.

literal: Their confessions implicated many in the imperial clan and those who had been coerced; therefore the chief villain Buhu was beaten to death, and the rest were all pardoned and released.
idiomatic: Their testimony dragged in many clansmen and men who had been forced along; the ringleader Buhu was beaten to death, and all the rest were forgiven and freed.

literal: Yuyue Shuilian's son Huage repeatedly harbored treacherous designs; the Emperor always treated him with forbearance, yet he turned back again and would not repent; summoning elder leaders and ministers to fix his guilt, both he and his son were executed, and their property was divided to supply the guards.
idiomatic: Huage, son of Yuyue Shuilian, nursed treason again and again; the Emperor repeatedly indulged him, yet he relapsed and would not mend. Elders and ministers were summoned to judge his crime; he and his son were both slain, and their goods were split among the guards.

literal: The officials had interrogated more than three hundred rebels; when the case was complete, the Emperor, considering human life supremely weighty and that the dead cannot live again, granted them a banquet for one day, allowing each according to his lifelong preferences.
idiomatic: The courts had tried more than three hundred rebels; when the dossiers were complete, the Emperor, holding life most precious and knowing the dead do not return, gave them one last feast, each man indulged in what he had loved in life.

literal: When the wine had deepened, some sang, some danced, some sported at archery or wrestling—each to the full of his desire.
idiomatic: As the cups went round, some sang, some danced, some shot for sport or wrestled—each to the limit of his wish.

literal: The next day, sentences were passed according to severity.
idiomatic: The next day punishments were meted out by degree.

literal: Chief villain Cige, next Dieci Ge—the Emperor still regarded them as brothers, unwilling to apply the law; he beat them and released them.
idiomatic: Cige was chief among the guilty, Dieci Ge next; the Emperor still called them brothers and could not bear the full penalty—he flogged them and let them go.

literal: Because Yindishi and Anduan were by nature mediocre and weak, used by Cige, all their guilt was released.
idiomatic: Yindishi and Anduan, being dull and easily led, had acted at Cige's bidding; their crimes were all remitted.

literal: The former Yuyue Hedili's son Jieli and Cige's wife Xiala Yi had truly participated in the plot; both were ordered strangled.
idiomatic: Jieli, son of the former yuyue Hedili, and Cige's wife Xiala Yi had truly shared in the plot; both were ordered strangled.

literal: Yindishi's wife Nieli had been coerced; Anduan's wife Nianmugu had once offered loyal advice—all were exempted.
idiomatic: Yindishi's wife Nieli had been forced along; Anduan's wife Nianmugu had once warned in good faith—both were spared.

literal: He then said to those nearby: "My younger brothers, though by nature clever and sharp, long stored treachery and accumulated wickedness.
idiomatic: He then told those at his side: "My brothers are quick and clever, yet they hoarded treachery and piled up evil.

literal: They once prided themselves on wisdom surpassing others; cruel and fierce without qualm; gorges and ravines may be filled, yet greed and corruption know no satiety.
idiomatic: They boasted of wisdom above other men, ruthless and savage without restraint; though gorges may be filled, their greed never knew its fill.

literal: Seeking others' faults—even small ones that could be forgiven—they called as weighty as Mount Tai;
idiomatic: Hunting others' faults, they treated the smallest slip, easily pardoned, as heavy as Mount Tai;

literal: their own unrighteous conduct, even entering into great evil, they deemed lighter than a goose feather.
idiomatic: their own wrongdoing, even when it sank into deepest crime, they called lighter than a goose down.

literal: Clinging to petty men, plotting with women, aiding one another in evil, thereby endangering the fate of the state.
idiomatic: They kept company with low men, schemed with women, and helped one another in wickedness until the throne itself was threatened.

literal: Even if one wished them not to fail—how could it be attained?
idiomatic: If one wished them not to ruin themselves—how could such a wish be granted?

literal: Northern Chancellor Shilu's wife Yuludugu was among the nation's closest kin; in a single day she betrayed me and joined the rebellion; before law could be applied she died of illness.
idiomatic: Northern Chancellor Shilu's wife Yuludugu stood among my nearest kin; in a day she turned against me and joined the rebels; before sentence could fall, sickness took her.

literal: This was Heaven's punishment.
idiomatic: That was Heaven's judgment.

literal: Jieli from youth constantly shared bed and board with me; the favor shown him topped all the clan; yet together with his father he turned against great kindness to follow wrong paths—can this be forgiven!"
idiomatic: Jieli from boyhood ate and slept at my side; no kinsman knew a kindness like his—yet he and his father repaid deep grace with rebellion. How could that be forgiven!"

literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the bingshen new moon, officials submitted the charges of more than three hundred clansmen who plotted rebellion; all were executed in the marketplace.
idiomatic: In the seventh autumn month, on the bingshen new moon, the courts reported the crimes of more than three hundred tent-kin who had joined the plot; all were put to death in the market.

literal: The Emperor sighed: "Bringing men to death—how is that what I desire?
idiomatic: The Emperor sighed: "To send men to their deaths—is that my wish?

literal: Had they only wronged my person, pardon might still be granted.
idiomatic: Had they merely wronged me alone, mercy might still have been possible.

literal: This lot wantonly pursued the wayless path, slaughtered the loyal and good, scorched the living people, plundered property.
idiomatic: But this crowd ran riot in lawlessness, butchered the loyal, burned the people alive, and stripped their goods.

literal: Among the people, where once there were ten thousand horses, all now went on foot—unprecedented since the founding of the state.
idiomatic: Where the commons once kept ten thousand horses between them, now all went on foot—a thing never seen since the realm was founded.

literal: Truly there was no choice but to put them to death."
idiomatic: I had no choice but to kill them."

literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiazi new moon, the Kaihuang Hall was built on the foundation of the Bright King Tower.
idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, on the jiazi new moon, Kaihuang Hall was raised on the old site of the Bright King Tower.

literal: In the ninth year, in the first month of spring, the Wugu tribe rebelled; he campaigned and pacified them.
idiomatic: In the ninth year, in the first spring month, the Wugu tribe rose; he marched against them and brought them to heel.

literal: In the sixth month of summer, Youzhou military officer Qi Xingben led his clan and his followers—men and women, three thousand in all—to request surrender; by decree he was appointed Acting Minister of the Secretariat, Left Vice Director, granted the name Wuyu, and supplied with rations.
idiomatic: In the sixth summer month, Qi Xingben, an officer of Youzhou, came over with his clan and retainers, three thousand souls in all; by edict he was named Acting Minister of the Secretariat and Left Vice Director, given the name Wuyu, and granted provisions for his people.
